data.name: Ashiqa
data.gender_notes: Ashiqa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A term used to describe a strong and intense love in Arabic literature, often used to describe the love between a mumin (believer) and Allah. The name Ashiqa carries the meaning “Passionate love” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashiqa usually hope their child will grow to embody passionate love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The love and devotion of a believer for Allah and His Prophet (peace be upon him).
data.etymology: Ashiqa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Passionate love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashiqa total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Ashiqa" holds a significant place in Arabic literature where it is used to describe a passionate and intense love. This term has been used in poetry and literature to express the deepest and most profound form of love. In contemporary context, it is often used to describe a devoted and ardent love for someone or something. In some contexts, it can also be used metaphorically to describe the love of beauty, art, or even country.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the term "Ashiqa" takes on a deeper spiritual meaning as it is used to describe the intense and passionate love that a believer (mumin) has for Allah. This love is not just about obedience and fear, but also about tenderness, longing, and yearning for the divine. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) once said, "None of you will enter Paradise until he loves me, may Allah raise me high." This love for the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and Allah is the essence of being a mu'min, and it is this love that invites us to greater levels of devotion, faith, and closeness to the Divine.
